subject: Accounting
question:
The trial balance of Alhaji Jingi as at 31st December, 2014 did not balance. The following errors were discovered:
i. The sales account was under cast by ₦15,900
ii. Discount allowed of ₦550 was not recorded at all
iii. Motor vehicle repairs of ₦3,720 was debited to motor vehicles account as well as the motor vehicle repairs account
iv. Credit purchases from Mallam Soji for ₦25,000 were debited to discount received account and credited to Mallam Choji account
v. Bank charges of ₦3,200 were debited to miscellaneous expenses only with no credit entry
vi. ₦182, 000 was paid to a creditor in full settlement of ₦ 85,000 owed. The debtors account was credited with ₦182, 000 owed. The debtors account was credited with ₦182,000 while discount allowed was debited with ₦3,000
vii. Furniture purchased on credit for ₦275,000 was recorded by only crediting the furniture account
viii. The balance of ₦775,000 on sales return account was listed as ₦755,000
You are required to:
a. Determine the difference between the totals of the two columns, by clearly indicating the difference caused by each error and
b. Prepare the suspense account to correct these errors
(18marks)
modelAnswer:
Note on error (vi): the wording is garbled; it mixes a payment to a creditor with entries in the debtors account, and the amounts do not match. It is taken to mean: ₦182,000 was received from a debtor in full settlement of ₦185,000 owed; the debtor's account was credited with ₦182,000, and discount allowed was debited with ₦3,000, but the matching ₦3,000 credit to the debtor's account was never made.

(a) Effect of each error on the trial balance
(i) Sales under-cast by ₦15,900: the credit column is understated, so the debit column exceeds the credit column by ₦15,900.
(ii) Discount allowed of ₦550 not recorded at all: an error of omission; no effect on the totals.
(iii) Repairs of ₦3,720 debited to both motor vehicles and motor vehicle repairs: an extra debit, so the debit column is too high by ₦3,720.
(iv) Purchases from Soji debited to discount received and credited to Choji: both a debit and a credit of ₦25,000 were made (wrong accounts), so there is no effect on the totals.
(v) Bank charges of ₦3,200 debited to miscellaneous expenses with no credit: the credit to bank is missing, so the debit column exceeds the credit column by ₦3,200.
(vi) Discount allowed of ₦3,000 debited, but the debtor not credited: the debit column exceeds the credit column by ₦3,000.
(vii) Furniture of ₦275,000 bought on credit, recorded only as a credit to furniture: there is a credit of ₦275,000 with no debit, so the credit column exceeds the debit column by ₦275,000.
(viii) Sales returns of ₦775,000 listed as ₦755,000: the debit column is understated by ₦20,000, so the credit column exceeds it by ₦20,000.

Net difference:
Errors making the debit column larger: ₦15,900 + ₦3,720 + ₦3,200 + ₦3,000 = ₦25,820
Errors making the credit column larger: ₦275,000 + ₦20,000 = ₦295,000
The credit column exceeds the debit column by ₦295,000 − ₦25,820 = ₦269,180.
A suspense account with a debit balance of ₦269,180 was therefore needed to make the trial balance agree.

Correcting journal entries:
(i) Dr Suspense ₦15,900; Cr Sales ₦15,900
(ii) Dr Discount allowed ₦550; Cr Debtors ₦550 (no suspense entry)
(iii) Dr Suspense ₦3,720; Cr Motor vehicles ₦3,720
(iv) Dr Purchases ₦25,000; Cr Discount received ₦25,000; and Dr Mallam Choji ₦25,000; Cr Mallam Soji ₦25,000 (no suspense entry)
(v) Dr Bank charges ₦3,200; Cr Miscellaneous expenses ₦3,200; and Dr Suspense ₦3,200; Cr Bank ₦3,200
(vi) Dr Suspense ₦3,000; Cr Debtor ₦3,000
(vii) Dr Furniture ₦550,000 (to cancel the wrong credit of ₦275,000 and record the correct debit of ₦275,000); Cr Creditor (supplier) ₦275,000; Cr Suspense ₦275,000
(viii) Dr Sales returns (in the trial balance listing) ₦20,000; Cr Suspense ₦20,000

(b) Suspense Account
Debit side:
Difference in trial balance: ₦269,180
Sales (i): ₦15,900
Motor vehicles (iii): ₦3,720
Bank (v): ₦3,200
Debtor (vi): ₦3,000
Total: ₦295,000

Credit side:
Furniture (vii): ₦275,000
Sales returns (viii): ₦20,000
Total: ₦295,000

The suspense account is cleared (both sides total ₦295,000), which confirms the corrections.
